title: What the compiler checks in a switch expression

questions.stem: Per this page, what does the compiler do with a switch expression over an enum that leaves out one constant and has no `default`?

options.text: It warns about it, and the missing constant yields null
options.says: The page says a switch expression that does not cover every case is a compilation error, not a warning.

options.text: It accepts it, and the missing constant throws when reached
options.says: The page says the compiler checks exhaustiveness and gives a compilation error when a case is not covered.

options.text: It rejects it, and the missing constant must get a case first
options.says: The page says switch expressions must be exhaustive, and an uncovered case is a compilation error.

questions.stem: Per this page, where does control go once an arrow (`->`) case has finished?

options.text: Past the switch, even with no `break` written
options.says: The page says there is no fall-through between cases when using the arrow syntax.

options.text: Into the next case, unless a `break` is written
options.says: The page says arrow cases never fall through, so there is no next case to stop with break.

options.text: Into the `default` arm, even with no `break` written
options.says: The page says there is no fall-through between cases with the arrow form, so a finished case does not run on into the default arm either.
